Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Match items and fluids

Choose which molecule appears when a player hovers an item or fluid. Add selectors to a molecule definition, such as a water bucket or a fluid with a particular NBT tag, then register the definition. The rules below explain which match wins when several apply.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
items(selectors...) Item IDs, optionally with metadata and NBT Match existing item stacks; the examples show exact selector syntax.
fluids(selectors...) Fluid names, optionally with NBT Match fluid stacks using the supplied constraints.
matchContainers(true) Boolean flag Allow the container matching behavior described below.
build() No arguments Finish the definition with its matching rules; register it to activate those rules.

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.
Java imports 
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.molecule.*;

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.*;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import net.minecraft.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.nbt.NBTTagCompound;
import net.minecraftforge.fluids.Fluid;
import net.minecraftforge.fluids.FluidStack;

Pick the right selector

Pick the right selector
Selector / input Matches Does not require
minecraft:coal Every metadata variant of that item A particular damage value
minecraft:coal@1 Charcoal metadata 1 NBT
minecraft:potion@0#{Potion:"minecraft:water"} Metadata 0 plus the required NBT keys An exactly equal whole tag
water The water fluid, normalized to minecraft:water A tag or amount
water#{Grade:"pure"} A FluidStack whose compound contains that string Absence of extra keys
Nonempty ItemStack / FluidStack Registry identity plus retained metadata/NBT where applicable A fixed stack count or fluid amount

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeSpec pureWater() {
    // Extra NBT keys in a stack are allowed. Grade must be the string "pure".
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:pure_water").name("Purified water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
            .items("minecraft:potion@0#{Potion:\"minecraft:water\"}")
            .fluids("water#{Grade:\"pure\"}").matchContainers(true).build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static MoleculeSpec pureWater() {
    // Extra NBT keys in a stack are allowed. Grade must be the string "pure".
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:pure_water").name("Purified water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
            .items("minecraft:potion@0#{Potion:\"minecraft:water\"}")
            .fluids("water#{Grade:\"pure\"}").matchContainers(true).build();
}

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown. 

{
  "name": "Purified water",
  "smiles": "[H]O[H]",
  "items": [
    "minecraft:potion@0#{Potion:\"minecraft:water\"}"
  ],
  "fluids": [
    "water#{Grade:\"pure\"}"
  ],
  "match_containers": true
}
Tip NBT values have types. A numeric Grade:1 does not satisfy the string Grade:"pure". No tag means a qualified selector fails. Empty stacks do not match. Association methods such as items(...) replace their previous field, so pass all alternatives together.

Match fluid tags as well as the fluid name

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeSpec taggedFluid(Fluid water) {
    var stack = new FluidStack(water, 1000);
    stack.tag = new NBTTagCompound();
    stack.tag.setString("Grade", "pure");
    // The builder keeps the tag requirement. Amount is not a selector condition.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:pure_water").smiles("[H]O[H]").fluids(stack).build();
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static MoleculeSpec taggedFluid(Fluid water) {
    def stack = new FluidStack(water, 1000);
    stack.tag = new NBTTagCompound();
    stack.tag.setString("Grade", "pure");
    // The builder keeps the tag requirement. Amount is not a selector condition.
    return AvogadroApi.builder("guide:pure_water").smiles("[H]O[H]").fluids(stack).build();
}

public static MoleculeDef lookupFluid(FluidStack contents) {
    // Keep the FluidStack; passing contents.getFluid() would discard its tag.
    return AvogadroApi.serverView().find(contents);
}

Fluid amounts do not affect matching except that an empty stack fails. Container lookups pass through the contained stack and its tags. A bare Fluid query uses unqualified rules only.

Match fluid tags as well as the fluid name
Query If Grade is pure If Grade is absent
find(fluidStack) Qualified rule wins before unqualified rules Qualified rule is skipped
find(fluid) Tag is unavailable; use unqualified rules Same
Filled item with fluid-handler capability Resolve its contents, provided the chosen definition allows containers Same fallback order for contents
Match fluid tags as well as the fluid name
JSON association If Grade is pure If Grade is absent
fluids: ["water#{Grade:"pure"}"] The qualified association can match the actual FluidStack. The qualified association is skipped.
fluids: ["water"] An unqualified rule remains available as a fallback. The unqualified rule can match.
match_containers: true A filled item can use its contained fluid and retained NBT. The contained stack uses the same fallback order.

Know which match wins

Know which match wins
Priority Item lookup FluidStack lookup
1 Generated molecule item’s saved ID Matching NBT-qualified fluid rule
2 NBT selector: exact metadata before wildcard; more-specific NBT before later registration Direct unqualified fluid ID
3 Exact metadata, then registry-wide item Avogadro fluid tag
4 Avogadro item tag (earlier tag binding wins) Supported GregTech material binding/path
5 Contained fluid, when permitted Fluid-path fallback
6 Supported GregTech material binding/path —
7 Molecule-path fallback —

For fluid NBT ties, more required content wins, then later registration. Direct duplicate bindings and duplicate path fallbacks prefer later definitions. A matching qualified selector wins before a general selector. example:acetone may be a path fallback for other:acetone, so use explicit associations when ambiguity matters.

Give several items or fluids the same molecule

Use a named list when several items should show the same model. The water example groups water containers under one tag, then refers to that tag from the water definition. These are Avogadro matching lists, not Minecraft item registry entries.

Java · add this method to your class.

public static MoleculeBatch tags() {
    return new MoleculeBatch()
            .itemTag("guide:water_containers", false, "minecraft:water_bucket")
            .fluidTag("guide:water", false, "water")
            .register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:tagged_water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
                    .itemTags("guide:water_containers").fluidTags("guide:water"));
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

mods.avogadro.molecules.itemTag('guide:water_containers', false, ['minecraft:water_bucket'])
mods.avogadro.molecules.register('guide:tagged_water', [smiles:'[H]O[H]', item_tags:['guide:water_containers']])

JSON · one definition per file unless a different destination is shown. 

{
  "replace": false,
  "values": [
    "minecraft:water_bucket",
    "#guide:other_water_containers"
  ]
}

The JSON above is a tag file, saved as config/avogadro/server/data/guide/tags/items/water_containers.json. A molecule binds it with "item_tags":["guide:water_containers"]. Fluid tags use tags/fluids and fluid_tags. These are Avogadro dictionaries, not modern Minecraft datapacks or Forge ore-dictionary names.

Show a molecule for a GregTech material

{"smiles":"Cc1ccccc1","materials":["gregtech:toluene"]}

The legacy adapter targets GregTechCEu 1.12.2 2.8.10-beta. gtceu:toluene is an alias; this does not imply compatibility with GTCEu Modern or every GregTech fork. Without the integration, ordinary item/fluid matching still works. No material is created.

GTCEu 1.12.2 release 2.8.10 identifies itself as 2.8.10-beta in game. A material binding matches the material reported by GTCEu for each stack: iron ingots, dusts, plates and other iron forms share one definition. All five language integrations use the same material matcher. Register one of the following definitions in your normal registration phase, after importing io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.

Java
AvogadroApi.owner("chemistry").register(AvogadroApi.builder("chemistry:iron").smiles("[Fe]").materials("gregtech:iron"));
Groovy
AvogadroApi.owner("chemistry").register(AvogadroApi.builder("chemistry:iron").smiles("[Fe]").materials("gregtech:iron"))
Kotlin
AvogadroApi.owner("chemistry").register(AvogadroApi.builder("chemistry:iron").smiles("[Fe]").materials("gregtech:iron"))
Scala
AvogadroApi.owner("chemistry").register(AvogadroApi.builder("chemistry:iron").smiles("[Fe]").materials("gregtech:iron"))
ZenScript
mods.avogadro.Molecules.molecule("chemistry:iron").smiles("[Fe]").field("materials", "[\"gregtech:iron\"]").register();

For JSON packs, use {"smiles":"[Fe]","materials":["gregtech:iron"]}. The binding leaves GTCEu's material definitions and item registrations unchanged.

Add water, look it up, and remove your registration

Java · add this method to your class.

public static CompletableFuture<MoleculeView> registerWater() {
    // Replaces this owner's contribution only. Other owners are untouched.
    var batch = new MoleculeBatch();
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:water")
            .name("Water")
            .atom("O", 0, 0, 0)
            .atom("H", 0.7586, 0.5043, 0)
            .atom("H", -0.7586, 0.5043, 0)
            .bond(0, 1)
            .bond(0, 2)
            .items("minecraft:water_bucket")
            .fluids("minecraft:water")
            .generateItem(true));
    return AvogadroApi.owner("guide").replace(batch);
}

Groovy · same API; place methods in your script or client helper as described. 

static CompletableFuture<MoleculeView> registerWater() {
    // Replaces this owner's contribution only. Other owners are untouched.
    var batch = new MoleculeBatch();
    batch.register(AvogadroApi.builder("guide:water")
            .name("Water")
            .atom("O", 0, 0, 0)
            .atom("H", 0.7586, 0.5043, 0)
            .atom("H", -0.7586, 0.5043, 0)
            .bond(0, 1)
            .bond(0, 2)
            .items("minecraft:water_bucket")
            .fluids("minecraft:water")
            .generateItem(true));
    return AvogadroApi.owner("guide").replace(batch);
}

Add water, look it up, and remove your registration
Action API / behavior
Initial mod registration Reuse AvogadroApi.owner("yourmod") during common initialization
Update several entries owner.update(batch -> { … }); complete them in one commit
Replace your collection owner.replace(batch) replaces only that owner’s definitions/tags
Remove one / all yours owner.unregister(id) / owner.clear(); lower source layers can reappear
Read startup content registeredView(); excludes world-specific JSON
Read authoritative running-server content serverView(); empty before server start and after stop
Read local client overrides AvogadroClientApi.view(); client code only
Wait for registration Use the returned future; do not block an authority thread waiting for itself
Add water, look it up, and remove your registration
JSON authoring task How it works
Add a definition Save one object at config/avogadro/server/data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json. Its ID is namespace:path.
Change a definition Edit the same file, then run /avogadro reload with permission level 2.
Remove a definition Remove its source file and reload. A valid lower-priority definition with the same ID can reappear.
Override a common definition locally Use the matching assets/<namespace>/molecules path in client resources, then F3+T. This does not change the server view.
Query or wait for a loaded view JSON cannot query views or receive completion callbacks. Use Java or Groovy for runtime integration.

Tip Reload and synchronization retain full stack NBT and attachment metadata. Unknown registry IDs do not manufacture missing content; inspect logs and the current view when a binding seems ineffective.

Find the molecule for an item or fluid

After water is registered, these queries find it by molecule ID or by a matching item/fluid stack. Use the running server’s view for server decisions. Use the client view for previews, where the player may have selected a different local model. 

var view = AvogadroApi.registeredView();
var definition = view.get("my_mod:water");
var ids = view.definitions().keySet();
var match = view.find(itemStack); // Actual ItemStack, including metadata and NBT.
var authoritative = AvogadroApi.serverView();

val view = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.registeredView()
val definition = view.get("my_mod:water")
val ids = view.definitions().keys
val match = view.find(itemStack) // Actual ItemStack, including metadata and NBT.
val authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

def view = molecules.view()
def definition = view.get('my_pack:water')
def ids = view.definitions().keySet()
def match = view.find(itemStack) // Actual Minecraft ItemStack.
def authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

val view = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.registeredView()
val definition = view.get("my_mod:water")
val ids = view.definitions().keySet()
val matched = view.find(itemStack) // Actual Minecraft ItemStack.
val authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

val ids = Molecules.ids();
val matchId = Molecules.findItem(<minecraft:water_bucket>);
val fluidId = Molecules.findFluid(<liquid:water>);
val authoritativeIds = Molecules.serverIds();
// Unknown geometry IDs throw; take this snapshot only after registration:
val geometry = Molecules.geometry("my_pack:water");

Java view.get/find return null when absent. ZenScript match methods return an empty string. Query the server view for authoritative decisions; a client’s resource override must never decide a server action. A geometry snapshot remains immutable after the registered definition changes.
